input.quote: d) The forecasts provided by IBM, or agreed to by IBM hereunder, do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product.
input.rationale: No minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay or volume floor is imposed on us. Section 6.0 makes our purchase obligation subject to the Agreement and expressly does not authorize MSL to produce or deliver any Product absent an order; Section 11.2(d) confirms that forecasts "do not obligate IBM to purchase any Product"; Section 6.1 lets us "cancel any and all Purchase Orders against this Agreement at any time" (no cancellation charge where MSL is in default); and Section 13.2(e) states we "have no liability for unused flexibility." That matches the preferred position: we pay only for Products actually ordered. The only volume-related exposure is the Appendix 2 / Section 13.0(f) requirements-accuracy mechanism, under which we compensate MSL if forecast accuracy for a machine type falls below the stated threshold, calculated as a small percentage of the material cost of volume shipped. That operates as a capped true-up for MSL's reliance-based parts purchases rather than a shortfall penalty or minimum-volume commitment, so it does not create take-or-pay exposure; we note it in diligence only (the percentages are redacted, so the commercial team should confirm the bracketed figures). No redline required.
